what: What robustness would cost here, predicted before it was measured
written: 2026-08-22, before run_multiplication_cost.py had been run once

the_setting.t_over_n: 2/7 = 0.286, which is below n/3 = 0.333 and well below n/2
the_setting.why_that_matters: Goyal-Song-Zhu (CRYPTO 2020) give unconditional MPC with guaranteed output delivery for t < n/2 assuming broadcast, and note that at t < n/3 the broadcast channel can be simulated over point-to-point links. This deployment is in the stricter regime, so no broadcast channel has to be assumed.
the_setting.what_we_run: malicious-shamir-party.x, secure WITH ABORT. MP-SPDZ's README: 'malicious means that not following the protocol will at least be detected'.

predictions.quantity: field elements per party per multiplication, MP-SPDZ malicious Shamir, n=7 T=2
predictions.reasoning: Damgard-Nielsen style multiplication is one element to a king and one back, so 2 per party semi-honest. Malicious honest-majority Shamir adds a sacrifice or a batched check, which roughly doubles it.

predictions.quantity: THE HEADLINE. GSZ's 5.5 elements per party against what this engine spends
predictions.why_it_matters: 'Comes free' is a claim about a baseline. If the ratio is near 1, robustness is free against the baseline we actually deploy and the gap is an implementation. If GSZ is several times our cost, then robustness is a real bill here and the paper's title is about a different starting point.
predictions.falsifiable: a measured ratio outside 0.7x to 2.8x refutes it

predictions.predicted: flat in the number of multiplications, because the program batches them into one SIMD row
predictions.why: if rounds grow with the batch the harness is measuring depth rather than width and the slope is not a per-multiplication cost

what_this_does_not_measure: Accountability. Naming the party that cheated is a different property from not stopping, and nothing in this runner touches it. GSZ identifies a corrupted party or a disputed pair as part of its dispute-control machinery, which is why its worst case is 7.5 rather than 5.5 --- but that identification is towards the other parties, not towards an outside auditor, and public accountability in the sense of Rivinius et al. needs more.
